# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration (dual-run architecture), allowing per-user cutover with fallback capability. Migration proceeds in phases based on user cohort, with each phase gated by explicit entry criteria and monitored against halt thresholds.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (Internal + Opt-In Volunteers)
**Population:** 1% of users (~400 users) — internal test accounts and opt-in volunteer customers with low-complexity billing profiles (single currency, no active disputes, standard subscription plans).

**Entry Criterion:** New billing system has passed full parity testing in staging against a replayed sample of 90 days of production transactions with zero critical discrepancies, and the dual-write reconciliation job has run successfully for 7 consecutive days with <0.01% variance.

**Goals:** Validate end-to-end invoicing, payment capture, tax calculation, and dunning logic in production with real (low-risk) traffic. Confirm rollback path works for individual accounts.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Cohort (Segmented Rollout)
**Population:** 25% of users (~10,000 users), selected via stratified sampling across plan types, geographies, and payment methods (cards, ACH, invoiced/enterprise) to surface edge cases.

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 1 completed with zero Sev-1 incidents, support ticket volume for migrated accounts within 1.5x of baseline, and all Phase 1 users stable on the new system for a minimum 14-day billing cycle (covering at least one full invoice/renewal event).

**Goals:** Stress-test the system against volume and diversity of billing scenarios (proration, refunds, chargebacks, multi-currency, enterprise invoicing) before full exposure.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (Remaining Users)
**Population:** Remaining 74% of users (~29,600 users), migrated in weekly waves of no more than 10,000 accounts per wave to preserve monitoring granularity.

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 2 completed with all halt-metric thresholds respected throughout, reconciliation variance sustained below 0.01% for the full phase duration, and a documented go/no-go sign-off from Billing, Finance, and Customer Support leads.

**Goals:** Complete migration of the remaining user base while retaining the ability to pause between waves if issues emerge.

**Note:** The old billing system remains fully operational (read/write parallel or read-only fallback, per account) through the entirety of Phase 3. Decommissioning of the legacy system is explicitly **out of scope for Phase 3** and is scheduled as a separate, subsequent phase (Phase 4: Legacy Decommission) that begins only after a defined post-migration stabilization window (minimum 30 days) with no reopened billing incidents tied to migrated accounts.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment processor tokenization mismatch causes failed charges for migrated card-on-file users | Run a pre-migration token validation pass against the processor's API for every account before cutover, with automatic rollback to legacy system on failure | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Double-billing occurs if dual-run reconciliation fails to detect a user processed by both systems simultaneously | Implement an idempotency lock per account during cutover window and enforce single-system-of-record flag with automated conflict alerts | Billing Platform Architect
RISK: Tax calculation differences between old and new systems create compliance exposure in certain jurisdictions | Run parallel tax computation shadow mode for 30 days pre-cutover per jurisdiction and require Finance/Tax sign-off before including that jurisdiction in any phase | Finance/Tax Compliance Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by a spike in billing-related tickets during a wave, degrading response times | Pre-train support staff on new system flows, staff a dedicated migration support queue, and cap wave size to keep ticket volume manageable | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Data migration script corrupts or truncates historical invoice/payment history for a subset of accounts | Take full snapshot backups pre-migration and run automated record-count and checksum validation immediately post-migration for every batch | Data Migration Engineer

---

## Halt Metric

If the **reconciliation discrepancy rate between old and new systems exceeds 0.5% of transactions in any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout is immediately halted, no further accounts are migrated, and the current wave is investigated before any resumption decision is made.

---

PHASES: 3
